query: For the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and its equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets that are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain why their mechanical properties differ during deformation and failure when constituent count alone is inadequate? Specify a controlled comparison, predictions relative to the quinary baseline, the applicable boundary conditions, supporting evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.material_initial_state: Homogenized, water-quenched, equiatomic FCC single crystals of quaternary and ternary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived medium-entropy alloys (MnFeCoNi, CrMnCoNi, CrFeNi, MnFeNi, MnCoNi, and FeCoNi), grown by Bridgman or optical floating-zone methods, annealed for 168 h at 1273 or 1473 K, and machined into [1̄23]-oriented 2 × 2 × 5 mm³ compression specimens; previously studied CrMnFeCoNi, CrFeCoNi, and CrCoNi crystals were used for comparison.
generation.intervention: The study compressed the [1̄23]-oriented single crystals and determined the CRSS for (111)[1̄01] slip across temperature; it also performed strain-rate jumps, TEM of dislocations, and DFT calculations of mean-square atomic displacement (MSAD). CRSS–temperature data outside the inertial and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier regimes were fitted with a conventional thermal-activation equation to extrapolate CRSS to 0 K and compare it with solid-solution-strengthening models.
generation.conditions: Compression was conducted from 9 to 1373 K at an engineering strain rate of 1 × 10^-4 s^-1. Below room temperature, strain-rate jumps spanning 1 × 10^-4 to 1 × 10^-2 s^-1 were made during low-hardening Stage I deformation (about 10% plastic strain). CRSS was calculated from the 0.2% offset yield stress using a Schmid factor of 0.467. Fits excluded measurements below the alloy-specific critical temperature for inertial dulling and above 873 K where the PL effect contributes. For a mechanistic PL test, CrFeNi was compressed to about 3% plastic strain at room temperature and 1173 K and examined by TEM.
generation.structural_mediator: Increasing Ta-Nb-V changed the alloy from single HCP HZTX0 through a BCC-dominant state containing residual HCP and, at low addition (especially HZTX0.1), abundant hard and brittle omega phase, toward an essentially single-BCC structure at high x. Increasing x also refined/altered the grains, intensified Ta-rich dendrite/V-rich interdendritic segregation and lattice distortion, and at x = 0.9 produced a preferred <100> BCC orientation.
generation.mechanism: Ta, Nb, and V act as beta/BCC stabilizers, lowering BCC free energy and suppressing HCP and omega formation at sufficient concentration. At x = 0.1, omega-phase precipitation causes brittle fracture and extensive fragmentation. At larger x, atomic-size and modulus mismatch produces lattice distortion and solute-dislocation interactions that impede glide, providing solid-solution strengthening, although severe distortion can reduce ductility. During high-rate deformation, more than 90% of plastic work is described as converting to heat; adiabatic heating and thermal softening localize deformation into shear bands. Fragmentation exposes reactive Hf and Zr to atmospheric oxygen, causing rapid exothermic oxidation and visible sparks; finer, more complete fragmentation promotes stronger energy release.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to room-temperature deformation, cooling was expected to substantially raise CRSS, with the increase becoming less steep below about 77 K because of dislocation inertia. Relative to the nearly temperature-independent intermediate-temperature baseline, heating into the diffusion-active regime was expected to cause a small CRSS increase and serrated flow through the PL effect. Across compositions, larger averaged MSAD—especially in Cr-containing alloys—was expected to predict higher extrapolated 0 K CRSS, while greater Mn plus Fe content was expected to produce a larger PL increment.
generation.baseline: The principal temperature baseline was room-temperature CRSS for cryogenic strengthening; the high-temperature comparison was the flattened/intermediate-temperature CRSS before serrated PL flow. Compositionally, the quinary HEA and previously measured CrFeCoNi and CrCoNi single crystals, as well as Cr-free or lower-MSAD derivatives, served as comparisons. Thermal-activation extrapolations without low-temperature inertial dulling provided the reference for quantifying Δτ0.
generation.boundary: The findings apply to equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-based quinary, quaternary, and ternary concentrated solid solutions tested as [1̄23] bulk single crystals in compression. Conventional thermal activation describes behavior below room temperature except below alloy-specific Tc values of about 60–77 K, where inertia matters. PL strengthening occurs approximately from 673–973 K onward, depending on alloy, with peak CRSS at 1073–1273 K and onset at about 0.44–0.56 Tm. The MSAD scaling has noted deviations for CrFeNi and FeCoNi, possibly because the nonmagnetic 0 K DFT calculations omit magnetic transitions.

falsification_experiment.design: Temperature-dependent CRSS from 0.2% offset yield stress and slip-trace identification; peaks in strain-rate sensitivity and apparent activation volume from strain-rate-jump tests to identify inertial onset; stress–strain serrations and the high-temperature CRSS increment to identify the PL effect; TEM measurements of partial-dislocation dissociation width and inferred stacking-fault energy at room temperature versus 1173 K to test Suzuki segregation; and the correlation of extrapolated τ0/μ with sqrt(MSAD)/b to test lattice-distortion scaling.
measurements: Temperature-dependent CRSS from 0.2% offset yield stress and slip-trace identification; peaks in strain-rate sensitivity and apparent activation volume from strain-rate-jump tests to identify inertial onset; stress–strain serrations and the high-temperature CRSS increment to identify the PL effect; TEM measurements of partial-dislocation dissociation width and inferred stacking-fault energy at room temperature versus 1173 K to test Suzuki segregation; and the correlation of extrapolated τ0/μ with sqrt(MSAD)/b to test lattice-distortion scaling.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
